To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thermal dewetting of the SOI template layer is suppressed by heteroepitaxy with Ge and that this suppression is caused by the weakening of Si-Si bonds and the decreased surface energy anistropy of the Ge/Si interface.

Ge lowers the dewet temperature of the Si(001) template layer in SOI to 700 °C, and that Ge coverage gradually destroys long-range ordering of the 3D nanostructure along the ⟨1 3 0⟩ directions and decreases the shape anisotropies of 3D nanostructures in the dewetting process of the Si(00l) template layer in the SOI.

Ge coverage gradually destroys long-range ordering along ⟨1 3 0⟩ directions and shape anisotropies of 3D silicon nanocrystals during the thermal dewetting of SOI(0 0 1) templates, and Ge lowers the dewet temperature to as low 700 °C.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermal dewetting of Si(0 00) and the influence of Ge on the process.
the effect of germanium on the thermal deweting and agglomeraion of the Si(001) template layer in the thin SiO2-based SOI.
the influence of heterogeneously grown Ge on the dewetting and 3D nanocystallite agglomeration in ultrathin SOI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Ge has a strong influence on the dewetting and subsequent agglomeration process of the Si(001) template layer in SOI.
Ge is a very good candidate to control the Si dewetting and agglomerations.
Ge coverage reduces the dewetting and the agglomeration temperatures, and it gradually destroys the long-rang ordering of 3-D nanocrystals and the shape anisotropies of 3-D Si nanocrystals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Ge is a good candidate for the formation of ultrathin SOI templates for nanowire fabrication, as it lowers the dewetting/agglomeration temperature, and it is also compatible with the fabrication of Ge/Si nanowires.
the Ge coverage is an important parameter to control the dewetting and the resulting 3D nanostructures in SOI.
Ge has the potential to control the morphology of 3D Si nanocrystals in SOI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ge can be used as a catalyst to lower the dewetting temperature of ultrathin SOI(0 0 1) layers.
Ge can be used to tune the dewetting temperature of ultrathin Si films in SOI and thus to control the size and shape of the Si nanocrystals.
Ge can be used to tailor the thermal dewetting of Si(0 00 1) template layers.
